name: USS Colorado
shortDescription: Eight-gun all-or-nothing battleship, the slowest of her tier but the best armored and best protected against torpedoes.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 20s action, 80s cooldown, unlimited charges. Standard USN reset, the same cycle as Nevada's and New Mexico's.

consumables.name: Repair Party
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 28s each at 391 hp/s, about 0.66% of max HP per second against the standard 0.5%, roughly 32,900 hp back across all three charges against her 59,300 hp pool.

consumables.name: Enhanced Secondary Targeting
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 30s window, +100% secondary shell grouping and -50% dispersion, 160s cooldown. The accuracy pick in her Slot 3 pairing, though her 127mm secondaries are short-ranged and light enough that the buff has less to work with than it does on some other USN battleships.

consumables.name: Exhaust Smoke Generator
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 45s screen off a 150s cooldown, 10s to lay. An unusual option for a battleship this size, the Slot 3 alternative to Enhanced Secondary Targeting for breaking contact or repositioning instead of committing to a brawl.

strengths: 457mm max belt on the all-or-nothing armor scheme, tied with Nagato for the thickest of any tier VI battleship and well ahead of Gneisenau's 360mm, Sinop's 400mm, Lyon's 360mm, and King George V's and F. Caracciolo's shared 381mm
37% torpedo damage reduction, clear of every tier VI peer here (Gneisenau and King George V both sit at 22%, F. Caracciolo at 25%, Sinop and Lyon at 16%)
16.5 km gun range tied with Nagato for the longest at the tier, backed by 1.9 shell grouping that's tighter than all but Nagato's 2.0
640m turning circle, the tightest of the tier VI battleships and the official Agile trait to match
Upgraded AA suite adds up to roughly 294 combined DPS across three mounts, enough to make mid-tier squadrons think twice
Repair Party heals 0.66% of max HP per second against the standard 0.5%, which claws back some of what the smaller gun count costs her
weaknesses: 21 knots top speed, the slowest tier VI battleship here by a wide margin (every other one runs 26-32 knots), and acceleration without the top engine is bad enough that stopping or reversing is a real struggle
Only 8 guns across four turrets, four fewer than her own predecessor New Mexico's twelve, so landing the accuracy on offer matters more than raw volume
Dispersion gets inconsistent both past 14 km and inside 6 km
Poor secondary batteries, just 127mm mounts on a 5 km leash
26mm plating outside the belt like every tier VI battleship, so HE spam and overmatch from 380mm-plus guns still get through, and the tall superstructure catches a lot of it
tips: Angle the belt early and hold it. The all-or-nothing layout gives you a real immune zone as long as you're not showing broadside.
Don't count on speed to get you out of a bad spot, you're the slowest hull at the tier so commit to a position before you're already in range.
Pick your Slot 3 consumable around the match plan: Enhanced Secondary Targeting if you're planning to brawl, Exhaust Smoke Generator if you'd rather have an escape option in your pocket.
Look for the 6-14 km band where your dispersion is at its best rather than sitting at max range or rushing in close.
Keep Damage Control Party ready for the superstructure, it catches fire easily even though the belt itself is tough.

threats.reason: 380mm-plus guns punch through her upper hull and superstructure even though the belt itself holds up fine.

threats.threat: Faster battleships and cruisers dictating range
threats.reason: 21 knots means she can't chase a fight or reposition out of one, every tier VI peer here outruns her.

threats.threat: Destroyers closing for a torpedo run
threats.reason: 37% torpedo reduction softens the hit but her top speed still can't out-maneuver a well-aimed spread.

summary: Eight 406mm guns in four turrets, accurate at range and hard-hitting up close, but the slowest hull at tier VI by a wide margin.
All-or-nothing 457mm belt and 37% torpedo reduction make her the best-armored, best-protected tier VI battleship against both shells and fish.
A strong upgraded AA suite and a heal-heavy Repair Party offset a smaller gun count and weak secondaries.
playstyle.detail: Colorado gave up speed for everything else. She can't chase a fight or run from one, and her acceleration off a standing start is genuinely bad, but angle that 457mm belt and very little gets through until someone finds the thinner plating above it. Eight guns is light for the tier, yet tight 1.9 shell grouping and 16.5 km range mean the shots she does land tend to count, and the torpedo protection is the best around at tier VI if a destroyer gets a spread off anyway. The AA suite is unusually strong for a battleship this tier, so carriers and spotter planes don't get an easy pass. Pick a lane, angle in, and let the Repair Party make up some of what the light broadside costs you.

goalTags.note: 457mm max belt ties Nagato for the thickest at tier VI, and 37% torpedo damage reduction beats every other tier VI battleship here.
Roughly 294 combined AA DPS across three upgraded mounts, among the strongest AA fits of any tier VI battleship.
